accepted_claims: credited boundary-dual simplicial criterion and <=20 corollary with published classification input
remaining_gap: Construct a no-Steiner Hamiltonian-path tetrahedralization for every remaining degree-at-least-four core, including nonsimplicial polytopes, or give a counterexample excluding every tetrahedralization.

claims.statement: Deleting and reinserting a degree-three vertex preserves existence of a no-Steiner Hamiltonian-path tetrahedralization, including nonsimplicial and coplanar boundary cases.
claims.novelty: General-position predecessor is credited to Escalona-Fabila-Monroy-Urrutia; novelty of this degeneracy-safe extension is not asserted.

claims.statement: A vertex-minimal counterexample to the original convex-polytope path problem, if one exists, has minimum degree at least four.

There is a seven-vertex general-position family with Hamiltonian tetrahedralizations whose positive-volume limiting tetrahedra form a nontraceable K1,3 dual. This does not disprove existence of another tetrahedralization of the limit.
Independent 2-to-3 replacement of a selected old tetrahedron and a degree-four cap tetrahedron can fail geometrically, even though the full polytope admits a Hamiltonian cycle tetrahedralization.

The boundary-dual method applies to simplicial polytopes without requiring absence of nonfacial coplanar quadruples; the published cubic-planar classification gives the at-most-20-vertex simplicial core case.
